    AI Overview
    National Vietnam War Veterans Day is observed annually on March 29 to honor the 9 million Americans who served during the Vietnam War era. In 2026, this day commemorates the 53rd anniversary of the last U.S. combat troops departing Vietnam in 1973. Events include wreath-layings at the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington D.C.. 
    Key Aspects of the 2026 Observance: 
    • Significance: It honors all who served, including those who did not receive a proper welcome home, and acknowledges the over 58,000 names on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial.
    • Events:
      A national ceremony takes place at the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., with notable speakers including the Secretary of War and Veterans Affairs Secretary.
    • 2026 Highlights: Actor Gary Sinise and Vietnam veterans are attending special events in Washington D.C., including a concert and ceremony.
    • Activities: Commemorations are held nationwide by the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) and The American Legion to honor veterans, their families, and the fallen. 
    The day was officially established by the Vietnam War Veterans Recognition Act of 2017.

    People also ask
    Why is March 29th Vietnam Veterans Day?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    March 29 is National Vietnam War Veterans Day because
    it marks the day in 1973 when the last U.S. combat troops left South Vietnam and the last prisoners of war were released. It honors the 9 million Americans who served during the Vietnam era, many of whom did not receive proper recognition upon returning home. 
    Key Reasons and History: 
    • Significance of the Date: On March 29, 1973, the U.S. Military Assistance Command, Vietnam (MACV) was disembarked, marking the formal end of U.S. combat involvement.
    • Official Designation: While first observed in 1974, President Donald Trump signed the Vietnam War Veterans Recognition Act of 2017, officially establishing March 29 as National Vietnam War Veterans Day
      .
    • Welcome Home: The day is specifically designed to recognize the sacrifices of veterans who often returned to a divided country without a proper "welcome home".
    • Commemoration: It honors all who served between Feb. 28, 1961, and May 7, 1975, and encourages the display of the U.S. flag to thank these veterans, as stated on the PVA.org website and reported by Stars and Stripes.
